Most Powerful Harley-Davidson Road Glide Gets Even Meaner for the 2027 Bagger World Cup
19 photos
Photo: Harley-Davidson
Here we are, at the end of the first-ever season of Harley-Davidson's first international one-make racing series. It proved to be a very successful one, it seems, with the bike maker claiming a combined attendance for the season of some 800,000 people, witnessing, over the course of six rounds, five different race winners, podium finishes for each participating team, and a fight for the title between four riders that extended into the final round.
It was only natural, thus, that the company would continue this event. In fact, it even announced it is exiting King of the Baggers , the U.S.-only racing series for baggers, to focus on this new project. Confirmation of a second season of the Bagger World Cup came this week during the EICMA show in Milan, Italy, and brought with it news of an expanded calendar, more teams, and, most importantly, a revised racing motorcycle.
The Bagger World Cup only allows trace-prepped Road Glides to line up on the starting grid, and that is what will happen during the 2027 season as well. Using lessons learned in the races this year, and input from the riders, the already insane beast became even meaner.
Photo: Harley-Davidson As presented last year, the DynoJet-prepped racer was fitted with a 131ci Screamin’ Eagle Milwaukee-Eight 131R V-twin engine whose racing ECU and dedicated mapping allowed it to develop over 200 horsepower and over 220 Nm of torque, enough for it to get to a top speed of 191 mph (300 kph) pretty fast.
That doesn't seem enough for the upcoming season, so Harley announced some changes that could make all the difference in the upcoming races. The upgrades target engine performance, the transmission, suspension, electronics, and durability.
When it comes to the Milwaukee-Eight, Harley speaks of the new Road Glides gaining up to three percent more power, and an increase in the rev limit from 7,000 to 7,200 rpm. The transmission the engine is tied to, on the other hand, gets a new Dynojet quickshifter sensor.
On the suspension front, Harley went for new fork caps that should allow for an increased ride height at the front, imagined independently adjustable damping settings for the rear shocks, and improved the swingarm to help the rear wheel with grip.
Photo: Harley-Davidson The other major change made to the racer includes the fitting of an active tire pressure monitoring system, but three more are on the way: updates to the bodywork and improved rider ergonomics with changes to the handlebar controls, foot positions and seating configurations.
Because all teams in this competition race the same bikes, all the changes mentioned above will be made available to all participating teams. Speaking of which, we know at the time of writing there will be five of them fielding 11 motorcycles, but more are likely to join the party before the second season kicks off.
Confirmed, for now, are teams Joe Rascal (which will line up three motorcycles), Saddlemen Race Development (also three motorcycles), Niti Racing (three bikes), Kyle Wyman Racing (one bike), and Mad Monkey / Tobacco Road Harley-Davidson (one bike). As a reminder, this season's winner was Joe Rascal's Archie McDonald.
Now officially titled the FIM Harley-Davidson Bagger World Cup Tuned by Dynojet, the competition will continue to be held in conjunction with MotoGP weekends, with each outing consisting of two full-points races, one qualifying session and two free practice sessions. That means we'll get a total of eight circuits and double the number of races.
Photo: Harley-Davidson Below you can have a look at the venues and the dates where the Road Glides will make a spectacle next year:
Round 1 | April 23–25 – MotoGP Grand Prix of the United States, COTA Round 2 | May 14–16 – MotoGP Grand Prix of France, Le Mans Round 3 | May 28–30 – MotoGP Grand Prix of Italy, Mugello Round 4 | June 11–13 – MotoGP Grand Prix of Catalonia, Barcelona Round 5 | June 25–27 – MotoGP Grand Prix of the Netherlands, Assen Round 6 | August 27–29 – MotoGP Grand Prix of Austria, Red Bull Ring Round 7 | September 17–19 – MotoGP Grand Prix of Aragón, MotorLand Aragón Round 8 | October 1–3 – MotoGP Grand Prix of Portugal, Portimão
Harley expects the crowd of people who will be in the stands for all of these races to grow by some 60 percent, reaching 1.3 million. That's probably owed to the three new destinations that have joined the calendar for next year, the ones in France, Spain , and Portugal.
Although the start of the second season of the Bagger World Cup is still some six months away, Harley is already selling early bird tickets for the COTA race, offering a 3-Day Harley-Davidson Bagger World Cup Fan Experience Pass for $149. The offer is limited, but the bike maker does not mention when it will expire - we'll keep an eye on things and report back once we know more.
